items.question: How do I remove a logo from an image?
items.answer: Choose a photo or graphic you own or are allowed to modify, then upload it to WatermarkGemini. After Google sign-in, review the processing charge and start the cleanup. Inspect the former logo area for distortion before downloading the edited JPG.

items.question: Can I remove a logo from an image online for free?
items.answer: Eligible standard image tasks can use limited free uses. Additional processing may require credits, and Google sign-in is required. The workspace displays the available allowance or cost before you run the removal, so it is not an unlimited free service.

items.question: Can AI remove a company logo from a product image?
items.answer: It can attempt to clean a visible mark on an image you own or are authorized to modify, such as an old logo on an approved mockup. Check packaging curves, fine text and shadows afterward. Removal does not transfer rights to another company’s photograph or trademark.

items.question: How can I erase a logo without cropping?
items.answer: A targeted cleanup can keep the frame intact rather than removing the edge of the picture. Compare the output dimensions and composition with the original. Results may vary when the mark overlaps a face, patterned fabric or complex product edge.

items.question: Can a logo be removed without a blurred patch?
items.answer: The tool aims to blend the edited logo area with nearby image details, but an exact pixel reconstruction cannot be guaranteed. A logo over reflective or highly patterned surfaces may leave visible artifacts; zoom in on those areas before approving the result.

items.question: What if the logo is embroidered on clothing?
items.answer: Clothing logos may be woven into a repeating texture rather than sitting above it. Use a clear original image and inspect threads, folds and lighting after processing. If the edit damages important clothing details, it may be better to retake or re-render the approved product photo.

items.question: Can I remove an AI generator logo from an image?
items.answer: For an authorized file, you can try cleaning a visible AI-generated mark. Not all marks share the same design or position, and some files also include separate provenance metadata. This logo tool does not promise to remove invisible watermarks or creator credentials.

items.question: Can I remove a logo and text together?
items.answer: Both are visible elements, but an image with multiple marks may need careful review. Do not remove mandatory legal notices, usage information or attribution. Check all affected areas before downloading and keep the unchanged original for reference.

items.question: Which image formats are supported?
items.answer: The current tool accepts JPG, PNG and WebP images up to 10 MB and returns a JPG. PDF pages, layered design files and entire videos are not accepted as editable native documents by this image workflow.

items.question: Is it legal to remove a logo from a picture?
items.answer: It depends on your rights to the image and how you plan to use it. Cleaning your own outdated branding may be legitimate; stripping attribution from unlicensed stock or another creator’s content is different. Obtain permission or an authorized clean source when necessary.

items.question: How are uploaded images handled?
items.answer: Selecting a file locally does not upload it. After sign-in and submission, the file and result use temporary private storage and are generally scheduled to expire after about 24 hours. Check the privacy policy if the material is confidential.

items.heading: Remove Old Brand Logos from Product Photos
items.description: Rebranding often means your approved product image still carries an outdated visual identity. Cleaning the old logo can help you prepare a revised mockup without re-shooting every object. WatermarkGemini aims to repair the visible mark while retaining product silhouette, lighting and surrounding colors.

items.heading: Clean Logos Without Cutting Off the Picture
items.description: Cropping a corner logo can remove useful space, packaging or part of your subject. A targeted edit lets you keep the original image boundaries, which matters for square product listings and presentation graphics. Inspect whether the original aspect ratio and key objects remain intact.
items.imageAlt: Branded tote with corner logo; cropped alternative versus full-frame cleaned photo.

items.heading: Handle Fabric, Wood and Reflective Surfaces Carefully
items.description: A mark woven into a shirt or printed on a reflective bottle is harder than a flat overlay. Background textures, highlights and object edges may need careful reconstruction. Use a high-resolution source when possible, and examine the removal area before deciding the edit is ready for use.
items.imageAlt: Close-up sweater fabric with embroidered badge; detailed grain comparison.
